title: Rabbi Gamliel bar Ininua or Anya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned only in the Jerusalem Talmud. He was the colleague of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, as at the beginning of Peah, chapter 1: “Rabbi Gamliel bar Ininua and Rabbi Abba bar Kahana — one said … and the other said,” etc. He was a student of Rabbi Mana (I), as at the beginning of Peah, chapter 1, where he asked before Rabbi Mana. In Ketubot 4:8 the reading is bar Anya; likewise in Yoma, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, “Rabbi Gamliel bar Inani asked before Rabbi Mana”; in Pesachim, chapter 1, beginning of halakhah 1, “Rabban (Hyman proposes: Rabbi) Gamliel son of Rabbi Inyona taught before Rabbi Mana”; and at the end of Niddah, chapter 3, “Debi (Hyman proposes: Rabbi) Gamliel son of Rabbi Liani asked before Rabbi Mana” — Hyman proposes son of Rabbi Inina.

notes.text: The supplied וחרגא is understood as the other. The Yoma sequence ר״נ ב ראינאני is read contextually with the surrounding Gamliel entry, without pretending those letters fully write Gamliel. All the Rabban/Rabbi and Liani/Inina corrections remain Hyman’s; the chapter/halakhah series is Jerusalem Talmud.

The two adjacent consulted Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 passages preserve Gamliel ben Ininiya, Rabbi Abba bar Kahana and the question before Rabbi Mana. The first passage has a Rabban form and the next Rabbi; titles are not globally harmonized. Hyman’s Mana-I assignment and the proposed corrections in the other books remain his.
